en.title: Bondical Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and old age, and to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets.
en.usage:
Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; hypercalcemia (a condition in which there is an excess of calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; kidney stones; severe renal failure; or hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: children who get plenty of sunlight and eat normal meals; premature infants; infants; patients with cardiac or circulatory system dysfunction, kidney disorders, or hypoproteinemia; or those with a history of kidney stones. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist if taking it together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, or the like occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Kyutenhul Soft Capsule
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness (while ill or recovering), and old age; to relieve peripheral circulation disorders and shoulder and neck stiffness during menopause, and numbness and coldness of the hands and feet (cold hands and feet); to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), beriberi, and eye fatigue; and to relieve angular cheilitis (inflammation of the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (lip inflammation), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (tongue inflammation), eczema, and dermatitis.
en.usage:
Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months of age; or severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: premature infants; infants; hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine); gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; cardiac or circulatory system dysfunction; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; gallbladder-related disease; liver disease; gout; kidney stones; disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, and pancreatitis, or patients who must be given lipid emulsions with caution; patients at particular risk from fat overload; or patients with a predisposition to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests, and may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if using it together with estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If any of the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist: stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), vomiting, nausea, loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), depressed central nervous system function, dermatitis, foul odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, becoming progressively heavier, or bleeding continuing for a long time.

en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins D, E, B1, B2, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness (while ill or recovering), growth periods, and old age; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; for beriberi and eye fatigue; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis (inflammation of the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (lip inflammation), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (tongue inflammation), eczema, and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
en.usage:
Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts; a history of an allergic reaction to soybean oil; hypercalcemia (a condition in which there is an excess of calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; kidney stones; severe renal failure; infants under 12 months of age; or hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: infants under 1 year of age; children who get plenty of sunlight and eat normal meals; premature infants; infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; cardiac or circulatory system dysfunction; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; kidney stones (present or a history of them); disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, and pancreatitis, or patients who must be given lipid emulsions with caution; or patients at particular risk from fat overload. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, levodopa, or estrogen-containing oral contraceptives. Consult a pharmacist if taking it together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If any of the following occur, or in patients deficient in folic acid, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, loose stools, constipation, rash, redness, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), depressed central nervous system function, dermatitis, foul odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected or becoming heavier, or bleeding continuing for a long time.

Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Warning: An overdose in children aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies. Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine), are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, are a premature infant or an infant, have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or localized (occurring in a specific area) colitis, have a cardiac or circulatory system disorder, a kidney disorder, hypoproteinemia, a gallbladder-related disease, liver disease, gout, or kidney stones, have had kidney stones, or have folic acid deficiency. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

It may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values, or interfere with the detection of blood glucose in urine tests.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa preparations. Consult a pharmacist if taking it together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during use and before and after use.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (congestion and reddening), hives, itching, photosensitivity reaction, abdominal and stomach pain, convulsions, fever, coma, upper abdominal pain, red spots, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat), depressed central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disorder, digestive disorder, low blood pressure, or pulmonary edema (swelling) appear, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected or becomes progressively heavier, or if bleeding continues for a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Children should take it under the supervision of a guardian.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Because it may reduce their absorption, take them at an interval of 2 to 3 hours.

If constipation, diarrhea, or the like appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, the growth period, and old age; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; and to supply calcium in calcium deficiency and other cases.
en.usage:
Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies. Those with hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, hypercalcemia (a condition of excess calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones, severe renal failure, or a hereditary condition such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet, are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, are a premature infant or an infant, have a cardiac or circulatory system disorder, a kidney disorder, or hypoproteinemia, or have had kidney stones. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist if taking it together with cardiac glycosides, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during use and before and after use.

If symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Mecoy F Tablet
en.efficacy: Used to supply vitamin E, B1, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and lactation, decreased physical strength during illness or after recovery, and old age. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used to relieve shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and coldness of the hands and feet during peripheral circulatory disorders and menopause. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness, and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
en.usage:
Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding, or if the medicine is for a premature infant or an infant. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Consult a pharmacist if the patient has a predisposition to thrombosis or is deficient in folic acid.

Children should take this medicine under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take levodopa while taking this medicine. Women taking oral contraceptives containing estrogen should consult a pharmacist.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, congested and reddened flushing, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, stomatitis, or the like appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If menstruation coming earlier than scheduled, gradually becoming heavier, or prolonged bleeding appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.caution:

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if the medicine is for a child who gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or breastfeeding, or if the medicine is for a premature infant or an infant, or if the patient has cardiac or circulatory system dysfunction or hypoproteinemia.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist if taking it together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during use and before and after taking this medicine.

Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, twice daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to a child, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist when taking it together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea or black tea, during and before and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling (swelling), diarrhea, gastric discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth), loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, hypotension, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, upper abdominal pain, coma, red spots, cardiac arrest (asystole), depressed central nervous system function, dermatitis, foul odor in sweat and breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorder, digestive disturbance, pulmonary edema, dizziness, or swelling of the face and legs (swelling) appears, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected or the amount increases or bleeding persists for a long time, or in the case of patients with folic acid deficiency, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, oral contraceptives containing estrogen, or antacids. en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for antacid action and the improvement of symptoms of gastric and duodenal ulcers, gastritis, hyperacidity, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and acid belching.
en.usage:
Adults and children aged 12 years and older: chew and take 2 tablets (1 g) at a time, three times daily, 30 minutes to 1 hour after meals.
If necessary, one additional dose may be taken before bedtime.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, or patients with Alzheimer's disease, hemorrhoids, fluid retention (swelling), toxemia of pregnancy, diarrhea, undiagnosed gastrointestinal bleeding, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if you have kidney impairment, are physically weak, are on a low-phosphorus diet, have a digestive or absorption disorder, are elderly, have symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding such as vomiting of blood or black stools, or are a woman who is pregnant or may be pregnant or a breastfeeding woman. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 2 weeks of taking it, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving this medicine to a child, administer it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take tetracycline antibiotics while taking this medicine. Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, ulcer treatments, digitalis preparations, chlorpromazine, lansoprazole, prednisolone, penicillin, quinolones, iron (Fe) salt preparations, or salicylates.

If constipation, diarrhea, or the like occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist when taking it together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene.
